messages:
Maria G: FYI the docs CI started failing on main after the MDX migration. Docusaurus build errors with `DuplicateIdError: duplicate id \"getting-started\"` when generating localized pages.
Sam T: saw this too when pulling main. Repro: `yarn build` -> fail. Seems to happen when an MDX include is nested in a list item.
docs-bot: lint: mdx-heading-ids -> detected duplicate heading ids across locales. Recommend explicit ids or run id-dedupe step.
Kevin L: quick workaround: add explicit header ids like `## Getting started {#getting-started}` in offending files. Not ideal for mass migration.
Ellie: I can probably write a small script to scan `.mdx` files and append numeric suffixes for colliding ids per locale, or generate explicit ids from file path.
Sam T: pushed a draft PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4277) that includes a detection script + a pre-build check. Script output example:
```
# bad-ids.txt
docs/en/guides/setup.mdx: getting-started
docs/fr/guides/setup.mdx: getting-started
```
It flags collisions, but doesn't auto-fix yet.
Maria G: ok good first step. CI should fail fast with that check so we can catch before Netlify deploy.
Kevin L: another unrelated failure: Netlify shows a trailing-slash redirect loop for `/docs/` -> `/docs/index` on localized builds. That's breaking some permalinks.
Ellie: I think the trailing-slash issue is from mixing absolute links to `/docs` and relative `./index.md` in translated manifests. We should normalize links during the MDX pipeline. I can prototype a remark plugin to rewrite links that point to directory roots into explicit `/index` targets.
Sam T: sounds reasonable. I'll split the work: PR-4277 will add the id-detection + lint rule. I'll open PR-4278 with the remark plugin for link normalization and a couple of unit tests.
Maria G: please include a short migration note under `docs/migration/README.md` so community contributors know to run `yarn docs:check-ids` before opening PRs. Mention the Netlify preview caveat.
Sam T: will do. Also adding a CI job `docs:ci-check` that runs the id scanner + the remark transform in dry-run mode.
Kevin L: for long-term we should consider using explicit ids in include templates where possible so the templates are stable across locales. I'll add a TODO in the repo board.
Ellie: example remark skeleton I used locally: ```js module.exports = function remarkNormalizeLinks() { return (tree) => { visit(tree, 'link', (node) => { if (node.url && node.url.match(/\/docs\/$/)) { node.url = node.url.replace(/\/$/, '/index'); } }); }; }; ```
Sam T: nice. I'll copy that into PR-4278 and add tests that simulate localized link graph.
Maria G: cheers — once both PRs land, re-run Netlify preview and check redirects. If green, we can backfill metadata for a few translated pages and merge. :thumbsup:
docs-bot: deploy preview queued: netlify/preview-1234 - waiting on `docs:ci-check`.
